projects.name: Kafka Keyword Launcher API
projects.shortDescription: Built a Kafka-based API reducing latency by 35% and enabling real-time keyword analysis
projects.detailedDescription:
I identified scalability and constant polling issues in the legacy keyword launcher module that were impacting microservice performance.

* Analyzed the system scope by understanding user workflows, data volume, and the lifecycle of keyword and UTM data flowing through the platform.
* Designed a scalable microservices-based architecture by mapping all major components and their interactions through system design.
* Implemented MongoDB (NoSQL) to efficiently handle frequently evolving keyword schemas and associated UTM information.
* Developed a push-based Keyword Launcher API to eliminate dependency on inefficient polling mechanisms.
* Integrated Kafka with multiple partitions to enable event-driven communication, significantly reducing load on downstream microservices.
* Used Redis to cache frequently accessed data and optimize response times for high-traffic requests.
* Built the service using Java, Spring Boot, and Spring Security to automate keyword compliance checks.
* Deployed the solution on AWS using EKS for container orchestration and scalability.
* Centralized application logs using Logstash and monitored system health and performance through Grafana dashboards built on key operational metrics.
* Reduced overall system latency by 35% and enabled real-time analytics through event-driven processing.

projects.name: EduOrch
projects.shortDescription: Ongoing Project: Building an on-prem agentic system that orchestrates Canvas LMS admin tasks for university educators — FERPA-compliant, Git-backed, and AI-driven.
projects.detailedDescription:
EduOrch is an ongoing project I am building at WPI to eliminate the administrative overhead educators face managing Canvas LMS, course content, and lab infrastructure.

* Designing a fully on-premises agentic orchestration system where educators interact via a natural language CLI — no direct Canvas UI needed for routine tasks.
* Integrating Canvas MCP (Model Context Protocol server) to give the AI agent read/write access to courses, assignments, pages, quizzes, and announcements.
* Using WPI's ARC Inference Cluster (on-prem GPU nodes) to host Llama 3.1 70B as the reasoning engine — keeping all data within WPI's network for FERPA compliance.
* Built a Canvas-as-Code model where all course content is stored as Markdown files in WPI's on-prem GitLab instance — Git history replaces manual versioning, and GitLab is always the source of truth.
* Implemented an edit task flow where the agent proofreads or transforms content, shows a line-by-line diff for educator approval, commits to GitLab, and pushes an unpublished draft to Canvas — with the old item tracked in a dangling pages manifest for cleanup.
* Designed a lab server health check tool using Paramiko SSH to validate assignment server readiness before students access them.
* All state — dangling pages, sync timestamps, action log — persisted in SQLite on the agent host. No cloud dependencies, no external API calls.

projects.name: MARS (Machine Assistance & Resolution System)
projects.shortDescription: Built a multimodal product-support agent for the Vulcan OmniPro 220 welder that answers grounded setup, troubleshooting, and safety questions using manual retrieval, OCR, structured tables, visual artifacts, and optional voice I/O.
projects.detailedDescription:
MARS is a multimodal product-support assistant I built for the Prox Founding Engineer Challenge to help users troubleshoot, configure, and safely operate the Vulcan OmniPro 220 welder.

* Designed the system as a grounded product agent rather than a generic PDF chatbot, focusing on high-value workflows like polarity setup, duty-cycle lookup, troubleshooting, and diagram retrieval.
* Built an offline knowledge pipeline that converts the owner manual, quick-start guide, selection chart, and product visuals into a local retrieval bundle with page text, targeted OCR, visual metadata, structured articles, and hand-verified tables.
* Implemented a FastAPI backend with Anthropic streaming tool use so the agent can decide which retrieval tool to call and answer from local evidence instead of relying on model memory.
* Used a lexical retrieval stack based on BM25, fuzzy matching, synonym expansion, and deterministic exact lookups for high-stakes facts such as duty cycles and polarity settings.
* Built a React frontend that supports streaming responses, artifact rendering, cited manual pages, images, interactive HTML widgets, Mermaid diagrams, and voice input/output.
* Added curated structured outputs so the assistant can return more useful artifacts than plain text, including tables, setup references, and troubleshooting visuals.
* Optimized the system for speed, inspectability, and groundedness by keeping the knowledge layer local and precomputed rather than parsing documents at request time.

The result is a domain-specific AI assistant that feels practical for someone standing next to the machine, not just impressive as a demo.

projects.name: TAARS (Talent Acquisition Agentic RAG System)

projects.detailedDescription:
I built an AI-driven portfolio chatbot to transform static portfolio websites into interactive, recruiter-focused experiences.

* Designed and implemented a custom RAPTOR two-file retrieval system (JSON knowledge base + lightweight index) inspired by Obsidian-style knowledge structuring, enabling efficient context lookup without heavy vector databases.
* Built a low-latency retrieval pipeline using keyword routing and weighted scoring (summary, tags, skills, recency) with zero LLM calls during traversal.
* Developed a FastAPI backend integrated with Valkey for session management, caching, rate limiting, and conversation logging.
* Implemented SSE-based streaming for real-time response delivery to improve user experience.
* Designed a multi-tenant architecture with API-key isolation, enabling multiple users to deploy their own chatbot instances.
* Built a plug-and-play React widget (Shadow DOM) for seamless embedding into any website.
* Optimized system cost by restricting LLM usage to final answer generation and caching frequently asked queries.

The result is a scalable, low-cost, and production-ready AI assistant tailored for recruiter interactions and portfolio discovery.

projects.name: Caveman-Compress (Semantic Memory Compression Tool)
projects.shortDescription: Built a Claude skill to semantically compress memory files, reducing token usage across AI sessions by ~45% without losing structure or meaning.
projects.detailedDescription:
I built Caveman-Compress to address inefficiencies in how AI systems repeatedly load large memory/context files.

* Designed a semantic compression pipeline that reduces natural language verbosity while preserving meaning, structure, and technical integrity.
* Achieved ~45% average token reduction across real-world memory files with zero loss of critical information.
* Built a hybrid architecture combining LLM-based compression with local Python validation to ensure correctness of headings, code blocks, URLs, and file paths.
* Implemented targeted post-validation fixes instead of full recompression, minimizing additional token usage.
* Ensured strict preservation of non-compressible content such as code, commands, and structured data.
* Packaged the tool as a reusable Claude skill and distributed via CLI (`npx skills add`) for easy developer adoption.

The result is a persistent cost optimization layer that reduces token overhead across every AI session while maintaining accuracy and reliability.
* Run npx skills add amrutsavadatti/caveman#feature/caveman-compress

The system acts as a scalable AI workforce, improving productivity and output quality through structured orchestration and multi-agent collaboration.

projects.name: RAFT consensus algorithm
projects.shortDescription: Building a distributed systems project implementing the RAFT consensus algorithm to deeply understand leader election, log replication, and gRPC-based inter-node communication in a fault-tolerant environment.
projects.detailedDescription:
I was learning Kubernetes in depth and discovered that it uses the RAFT consensus algorithm internally for coordination and fault tolerance. That made distributed consensus feel abstract but clearly foundational, so I wanted to understand it by building it hands on.

 I set out to build a RAFT based distributed system from scratch as a learning focused project, so I could observe leader changes, replication, and recovery instead of treating consensus like a black box.


* Phase 1: Built a Spring Boot and gRPC skeleton and containerized it with Docker to run multiple nodes locally like a small cluster.
* Phase 2: Implemented leader election with terms, voting, and heartbeats to understand how a leader is chosen and maintained.
* Phase 3: Implemented log replication to learn how distributed nodes stay consistent over time.
* Phase 4: Ran fault tolerance tests by simulating node crashes and restarts to validate leader failover and recovery behavior.
* Phase 5: Built a frontend visualization to make cluster state, leader status, and log progress easy to observe.
* Phase 6: Replaced REST polling with WebSocket live push for real time updates and a more responsive system view.

 The result is a demoable RAFT cluster with a clear visualization and real failure scenarios, which gave me practical intuition for how Kubernetes style systems maintain consistency and resilience.

projects.name: Custom AI Tool Server
projects.shortDescription: Built a custom AI tool server enabling extensible, secure, and reusable productivity tools through a standardized MCP-based interface, deepening hands-on experience with AI tooling infrastructure and API design.
projects.detailedDescription:
I designed and implemented a custom AI Tool Server to explore how AI systems can securely and reliably interact with real-world tools through well-defined interfaces.

* Built a custom MCP server in Python using FastAPI as the transport layer and Pydantic for strict schema validation, ensuring robust and predictable tool execution.
* Used the mcp library’s @server.tool decorator to define extensible and reusable tool endpoints, enabling clean separation between tool definitions and execution logic.
* Implemented a weather lookup tool integrating third-party APIs to demonstrate real-time external data access.
* Developed a statistical calculator leveraging NumPy and SciPy to support computational workflows within AI-driven interactions.
* Integrated Google Calendar with OAuth 2.0 to enable secure, automated event creation and scheduling.
* Focused on clean API design, extensibility, and security to support future tool additions with minimal refactoring.
* Gained practical experience in building AI-facing infrastructure, authentication flows, and multi-tool orchestration, strengthening understanding of how modern AI agents interact with external systems in production environments.
